title: Kolattam
summary: A stick dance of Tamil Nadu in which dancers in pairs or rings strike short painted sticks against their partners' sticks in changing patterns, stepping in time to a song.
howToPlay: Four places are lit: where the partners' sticks meet in the middle, high overhead, low, and the dancer's own two sticks crossed.
Strike the place a closing ring marks, on the beat, so the sticks meet there.
Keep a steady count: the pattern repeats like a circle going round.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and an extra stroke costs points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: Kolattam is danced in pairs and in rings. Each dancer holds two short sticks, and the clack of the sticks keeps the rhythm of the song.
credits: Tradition: kolattam of Tamil Nadu; patterns written for this game
